doc.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Talking about Monk Rowe's playing and Cannonball Adderley
summary: McKenna asks Rowe about his instruments and styles, and they talk about Cannonball Adderley and the Miles Davis sextet.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Well maybe the Celtics will come back. They have a good coach now, we’ll see what happens. Those were the glory days.
So Monk, are you doing some playing yourself?
Yeah, I’m a saxophone and I tinkle with piano.
Yeah. I understood that, but what style do you favor, do you like to be playing in a small group, a big band?
Well it’s interesting because I went through my kind of contemporary jazz period where I was listening to like Weather Report and all that.
Yeah. But I’ve always been a huge Cannonball Adderly fan.

He just, for me, he was it, and still is basically. But now my tastes are really ranging backwards into the kind of stuff that we’ll be hearing tonight. And a lot of it’s from doing these interviews and talking.
Not really. I was one of those people that started on clarinet but didn’t stay with it very long and hard to go back.
Do you play tenor and some alto?
But, oh, sure. So that’s why — a Cannonball freak, yeah. He was something else.
I got to see him a few times.
What about that group with Miles, wasn’t it Coltrane and Cannonball?
